protocol.eligibility: The goal was discovered before decision 450 in the common intact prefix.
protocol.primary_outcome: Mean reward sum over decisions 600--1349, among eligible episodes only.
protocol.statistics: Eight training-seed means are the replicates; paired t and exhaustive sign-flip tests, Holm within the three primary contrasts. All other comparisons exploratory.
protocol.current_code: Original mixed PGC code in every variant.
protocol.shadows: Two RNN states per branch, receiving its identical actual images/actions/rewards/current code. One has mixed goal snapshots, the other ordinary-grid goal snapshots.
protocol.common_prefix: All actions are copied from the intact branch for decisions 0--599. Sensor states, shadow states, rewards and hit records are checked exactly.
protocol.frozen_offset: Mean mixed-minus-grid hidden difference over decisions 450--599. Grand mean over eligible slots is separated from each episode deviation.
protocol.wrong_offset: Grand mean plus cyclic-next-eligible episode deviation, rescaled to the own episode deviation L2 norm; zero-donor failures are reported.
protocol.between_basis: First 10 eigenvectors of weighted episode-mean covariance from the prior independent 16-episode replay.
protocol.random_control: Fixed seeded rank-10 orthonormal basis in the complement of the between-episode basis. Its dynamic patch is rescaled each step to the corresponding between-basis patch L2 norm on that same branch experience.
protocol.feedback: Only episode_mean_feedback and wrong_mean_feedback overwrite grid-shadow h after each step; grid c remains untouched. All other patches affect the actor only.
caveats: A constant actor-only hidden patch is a fixed action-logit bias. A null rescue does not rule out recurrent or time-varying uses of episode information.
Between-subspace dynamic restoration includes moment-to-moment signals, not just average offsets.
All rescues reintroduce predictive information; none is a pure ordinary-grid success.
Feedback patches can leave the natural hidden-state range; violations are measured, not clipped.
The episode-specific offset comes from a finite past calibration window and remains frozen as goal snapshots update.
The global and wrong-episode controls use contemporaneous calibration from other batch episodes; they are diagnostic interventions, not a proposed deployable agent.
Eligibility is fixed before intervention from the common prefix. No future hidden activity enters calibration.

calibration.scope: Descriptive eligible-count-weighted averages of two calibration batches per training seed. Batch covariance fractions are averaged, not recomputed from pooled samples. These are mixed-versus-grid goal inputs within the same PGC-trained network, not comparisons of separately trained populations.

statistics: Eight training-seed means are the replicates. Primary endpoint: final 750-step (50-second) score among episodes eligible at calibration. Three primary paired contrasts and five exploratory contrasts form separate Holm families, each corrected separately for paired t and exact two-sided sign-flip tests. CIs are marginal 95% paired t intervals; plot errors are SEM. Full-episode score and calibration measurements are descriptive.
limitations: Only frozen PGC-trained networks are intervened on; this does not establish why their training outperformed grid-only training.
Offsets are estimated from the same episode prefix, frozen before the handoff, and use no later observations or rewards.
An episode-specific difference may reflect goal-by-context/history interactions; it is not necessarily a pure goal coordinate.
The fixed-offset primary tests modify the actor input only; they do not replace recurrent h/c or isolate all future recurrent effects.
Dynamic subspace rescue changes a time-varying signal and cannot by itself prove that constant episode-average shifts are causal.
The feedback arms also alter the next recurrent h input while leaving c unchanged; they are distinct exploratory interventions.
An effective rescue would demonstrate sufficiency under the tested intervention, not exclusive necessity or the full source of the PGC training advantage.
A failed rescue can reflect an inaccurate or nontransferable constant-offset approximation and does not prove that all contextual activity is irrelevant.
